title: Margaret Atwood, bird advocates say fight against Ontario island telecom tower is gaining steam
summary: Canadian author Margaret Atwood says she has heard a lot of public support for a full impact assessment of a proposed telecom tower for Pelee Island in southwestern Ontario. Atwood and other bird…

image.caption: Celebrated Canadian author Margaret Atwood cuts the ribbon at the opening of the Atwood Gibson Bird Centre in September. Atwood is honorary chair of the Pelee Island Bird Observatory. (Pelee Island Bird Observatory)

blocks.text: Windsor

Canadian author Margaret Atwood says she has heard a lot of public support for a full impact assessment of a proposed telecom tower for Pelee Island in southwestern Ontario. Atwood and other bird advocates are seeking to stop the planned 200-metre tower from going forward.
U.S. finance company building the tower says it has conservation in mind and has already consulted
Canadian author Margaret Atwood and other bird advocates say they’ve seen a swell of public support in their quest to stop a planned 200-metre telecom tower on Pelee Island.

The Pelee Island Bird Observatory (PIBO), which counts the celebrated novelist as an honorary chair, said Wednesday that in under a week, more than 27,000 people sent letters supporting a federal impact study of the project. The non-profit expects that decision by Jan. 19.
The letter writers’ fears, PIBO says, are the same as Atwood’s — that the tower’s height, lights and guy wires will hurt birds flying Canada’s southernmost migratory route.
“We are not done,” Atwood, who was born in Ottawa and turned 87 last week, said Wednesday. “We will keep going. We will see what happens and we’ll see that Canada does the right thing.”
Pelee Island, seen in this aerial photo, is in the western basin of Lake Erie in Essex County. (Photo courtesy Ontario-Canada-Travel)
DRW, a Chicago-based financial trading firm, plans to build the tower next year.

The company said in a statement this month that it’s committed to environmental protection. It also said it went through a public consultation period as part of a process with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.

items: Margaret Atwood joins other bird lovers to fight against a proposed 600-foot tower on Pelee Island

blocks.text: "We are committed to voluntarily installing best-in-class bird collision mitigation technologies alongside the lighting requirements for aviation security," DRW said in a statement.

"We have welcomed the Pelee Island Bird Observatory’s feedback on those plans. We will continue that dialogue as the project progresses, with a shared goal of protecting the birds that travel through Pelee Island."

But Atwood said she and others were blindsided when they heard about the tower this fall. It was right around the time the nearby Atwood Gibson Bird Centre opened. She spent years fundraising for the project. The tower would be about two kilometres away, on 1245 Centre Dyke Rd.
Caldwell First Nation says it was also not consulted.
Tower project went to council 3 years ago
Township bylaws show the tower project first came to local council in 2023 and was formalized further in 2025.

items: New home for bird migration science on Pelee Island, honours the legacy of Margaret Atwood and Graeme Gibson

blocks.text: PIBO has sent the township a number of requests for information, said director Matthew Gibson. It also hopes to appear before council on Dec. 8.

A council of five governs the island, a tourist destination that has a year-round population of fewer than 300 people. PIBO estimates about a million birds fly over the island as they cross Lake Erie at the confluence of two flyways.
CBC Windsor is pursuing comment from Pelee Island council members. Coun. Dean Robillard said he hasn’t “been given any information with regards to the tower.”
CBC Windsor is also pursuing comment from the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada, the agency that will decide whether a federal assessment is needed.
